sections.heading: History
sections.wikitext: Once known as a favored Titan of the [[Amazons|Amazonian tribe]] of female warriors, Feyone was often mistaken as human at a distance and would thus lure in would-be attackers. But the fact that Feyone was quite a bit more than human would become immediately obvious to whichever unfortunate foe was first to engage her on the battlefield, though said foe would rarely have time to process this realization. {{source|Huntik.com}}

sections.heading: Sophie's Feyone
sections.text:
Sophie Casterwill used Feyone as her last Titan against a number of Suits at Sutos Island. She was able to send one of them to the ground before going back to her amulet after two Suits fired a Raypulse spell at her. [Like Father, Unlike Son]

In an all out attack against a couple of Organization Suits that ambushed the Huntik team at Newgrange Passage Tomb, Sophie invoked Feyone alongside Icarus. Feyone was able to take out an Enforcer Titan with the assist of Icarus. [Home Turf]

Feyone was invoked by Sophie alongside Icarus and Sabriel to fight Zhalia Moon and her Kilthane inside the Castle of Vlad Dracul. [The Vampire Loses Its Fangs]

Deep in the Turkish forest, Sophie showcased Feyone and Sabriel to the Amazons upon them asking where her Titans were, surprised Sophie was a Seeker. [Ladies' Choice]

Inside King Solomon's Mines, in the battle for the Legendary Titan of Spirit, Feyone and Sabriel were used by Sophie to battle against the Professor and his Suits alongside several other Titans invoked by the Huntik team. Feyone was sent back to her amulet after being hit by an Enforcer's laser attack. [To Be Together]

Sophie's Feyone was used in the final battle against the Professor inside his castle in response to a Suit's Terrapede Titan. Feyone quickly got grabbed by Terrapede, being sent to her amulet after being hit by its blast attack. [The Divine Comedy] When faced against the Professor in his invocation chamber, Sophie again invoked Feyone alongside Hoplite. Feyone managed to strike Behemoth and later on, Tao, helping stall the Professor's ritual to invoke Overlos. [The Mission]

Feyone was used by Sophie inside a hidden observatory at the Tower of Nostradamus to fight with the Organization for the Scrying Glass. Feyone blasted a Suit and the container that held the Glass off Hoffman's hands, before being later taken out by his Rippleburst spell. [The Tower of Nostradamus]

Inside the Cave of the Casterwills, on a test to retrieve Sorcerel's amulet, Sophie pondered invoking Feyone and Icarus to take out Coralgolem and Undine. However, she gave up on the idea upon realizing that the test wasn't meant to test her fighting abilities. [Cave of the Casterwills]

Due to Feyone's notable agility, she was invoked once again by Sophie Casterwill to fight Rassimov's Legion by the Spiral Mark. Legion managed to grab her, partially assimilating Feyone and damaging her amulet. Upon Lok Lambert destroying Legion's amulet, all of the damage was reversed. [The Spiral Mark]

sections.heading: White's Feyone
sections.wikitext: Feyone, alongside [[Mallory]]'s Icarus,  was invoked by [[White]] to help them strike the Huntik team from above while they were reaching the coastline leading to the [[Cave of the Casterwills]]. She managed to hit Sophie Casterwill, who was trying to reach the two Titans with [[Hyperstride]], sending her back to the water. [[Dante Vale|Dante]]'s [[Metagolem]] threw Feyone off the edge of the elevated position by throwing boulders at her, and she was finished off by Zhalia's [[Kilthane]].

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.wikitext:
Feyone is equipped with the unusual combination of light armor and heavy weaponry. With little more than a helmet and leather protecting her from attacks, one would think this female brawler Titan was doomed to fall to a well-placed jab, but she leverages her lack of armor perfectly, moving with a speed and grace that no armor-clad Titan can match. Watching her dodge the strikes of her enemies is like watching a giant do gymnastics: it doesn't seem possible with her size, but Titans regularly surpass the expectations of humans. Feyone is also able to project an energy beam from her hands when outstretched. She carries herself with serenity both off and on the battlefield. She is also very skilled with her sword.

full_text:
Feyone is a Celtic-Irish warrior like Gybolg. Seekers in old Ireland used Feyone Titans to break through lines of enemy warriors so they could challenge the leaders directly. She is commonly invoked alongside Icarus.

History

Once known as a favored Titan of the Amazonian tribe of female warriors, Feyone was often mistaken as human at a distance and would thus lure in would-be attackers. But the fact that Feyone was quite a bit more than human would become immediately obvious to whichever unfortunate foe was first to engage her on the battlefield, though said foe would rarely have time to process this realization. [Huntik.com]

Sophie's Feyone

Sophie Casterwill used Feyone as her last Titan against a number of Suits at Sutos Island. She was able to send one of them to the ground before going back to her amulet after two Suits fired a Raypulse spell at her. [Like Father, Unlike Son]

In an all out attack against a couple of Organization Suits that ambushed the Huntik team at Newgrange Passage Tomb, Sophie invoked Feyone alongside Icarus. Feyone was able to take out an Enforcer Titan with the assist of Icarus. [Home Turf]

Feyone was invoked by Sophie alongside Icarus and Sabriel to fight Zhalia Moon and her Kilthane inside the Castle of Vlad Dracul. [The Vampire Loses Its Fangs]

Deep in the Turkish forest, Sophie showcased Feyone and Sabriel to the Amazons upon them asking where her Titans were, surprised Sophie was a Seeker. [Ladies' Choice]

Inside King Solomon's Mines, in the battle for the Legendary Titan of Spirit, Feyone and Sabriel were used by Sophie to battle against the Professor and his Suits alongside several other Titans invoked by the Huntik team. Feyone was sent back to her amulet after being hit by an Enforcer's laser attack. [To Be Together]

Sophie's Feyone was used in the final battle against the Professor inside his castle in response to a Suit's Terrapede Titan. Feyone quickly got grabbed by Terrapede, being sent to her amulet after being hit by its blast attack. [The Divine Comedy] When faced against the Professor in his invocation chamber, Sophie again invoked Feyone alongside Hoplite. Feyone managed to strike Behemoth and later on, Tao, helping stall the Professor's ritual to invoke Overlos. [The Mission]

Feyone was used by Sophie inside a hidden observatory at the Tower of Nostradamus to fight with the Organization for the Scrying Glass. Feyone blasted a Suit and the container that held the Glass off Hoffman's hands, before being later taken out by his Rippleburst spell. [The Tower of Nostradamus]

Inside the Cave of the Casterwills, on a test to retrieve Sorcerel's amulet, Sophie pondered invoking Feyone and Icarus to take out Coralgolem and Undine. However, she gave up on the idea upon realizing that the test wasn't meant to test her fighting abilities. [Cave of the Casterwills]

Due to Feyone's notable agility, she was invoked once again by Sophie Casterwill to fight Rassimov's Legion by the Spiral Mark. Legion managed to grab her, partially assimilating Feyone and damaging her amulet. Upon Lok Lambert destroying Legion's amulet, all of the damage was reversed. [The Spiral Mark]

White's Feyone

Feyone, alongside Mallory's Icarus, was invoked by White to help them strike the Huntik team from above while they were reaching the coastline leading to the Cave of the Casterwills. She managed to hit Sophie Casterwill, who was trying to reach the two Titans with Hyperstride, sending her back to the water. Dante's Metagolem threw Feyone off the edge of the elevated position by throwing boulders at her, and she was finished off by Zhalia's Kilthane.

Lucas' Feyone

Lucas used his Feyone Titan to fight the Huntik team at the Casterwill Library. Feyone aimed her energy beam at Dante Vale, but he was able to dodge it. She was then sent back to her amulet in a quick sequence of attacks by Sophie Casterwill's Sorecerel. [Chasing Void]

Focauld Casterwill's and Rue Guardians' Feyone Titans

After a long spell, the Rue Guardians, with Focauld Casterwill's help, were able to invoke several Feyone and Icarus Titans, along with a Coralgolem Titan, housed inside the Fortress of Iron Will to protect it from the huge Blood Spiral army trying to invade it. Upon seeing the many Titans, the Blood Spirals retreated from the battle. [The Spiral War]

Feyone Titans of unspecified Seekers

One or more Feyone Titans were once assimilated by Legion in the past, which made use of Feyone's attacks against the Huntik team when they were trying to ambush Rassimov. With Feyone's energy blast attack, Legion knocked Den Fears and, later on, Sophie Casterwill to the ground, surpassing her Honorguard spell. [Rassimov's Secret]

At a given time, an unspecified Feyone fought against DeFoe and one his Redcap Titans. [SAS-124] Other unspecified Feyone Titans have also been seen. [SAS-055][SAS-119]

With little more than a helmet and leather protecting her from attacks, one would think this female brawler Titan was doomed to fall to a well-placed jab, but she leverages her lack of armor perfectly, moving with a speed and grace that no armor-clad Titan can match. Watching her dodge the strikes of her enemies is like watching a giant do gymnastics: it doesn't seem possible with her size, but Titans regularly surpass the expectations of humans. Feyone is also able to project an energy beam from her hands when outstretched. She carries herself with serenity both off and on the battlefield. She is also very skilled with her sword.
